pr_body:
The column transformer didn't work in combination with FindOperators.
This correction does not perform a transformation on a FindOperator value

Fixes: #9381

pr_comments:
Your solution will not perform the required transformation on the `FindOperator`'s value, so eventually the query will be performed on the wrong (or rather unexpected), untransformed value. 

Or am I missing something?

@vlad-ostrovski can't tell at the moment. I will have a look at it tomorrow... But can you verify that the fix isn't working I'm your case. By adding a check to your transformer... So that the transformation is only executed when value is not an instance of FindOperator?
@ertl But i do need it to be transformed.. even if it's a FindOperator (JsonContains)

@vlad-ostrovski the value was not transformed, but the Runtime Error was eliminated, and the transformation was indirectly performed from the database. While this solution worked for me, I acknowledge that it is not the correct behavior and have since corrected it. Can you please review it?

Regarding the JsonContainsOperator and a JSON array, the transformation utilizes the entire array instead of each individual value for the transformation. However, I was unable to test this as it appears that the JsonContainsOperator does not support arrays as input.
This one is scary to merge, because I don't know how it can affect exist users usage.

Actually, the desired behavior should remain the same. If a transformer is not used, the code will not execute. However, if a transformer is implemented, the else branch within 'if' statement (SelectQueryBuilder.ts) will run, utilizing the same code as before. Prior to my modification, it was not possible to use FindOperators with a transformed column, which is an important issue that has now been addressed.

review_comments: Shouldn't be used here.. creates spaghetti

why not use the same approach already implemented in `SelectQueryBuilder` for `EqualOperator`s?
look one line above your change in `SelectQueryBuilder`

@vlad-ostrovski originally, my first approach was to recursively traverse the FindOperators in the parameterValue, but the value of a FindOperator is readonly. Therefore, I had to choose between making it writeable or exposing a transform functionality. Ultimately, I decided to go with the latter since I think it's more readable and provides the added benefit of inheritance (that you also have noted), allowing for different scenarios to be addressed for each operator.
